title: Your Pillow Has 8-Legged Roommates 🛏️ (Things Living In Your House #49)
pinned_comment: Honest answer: how often do you actually wash your pillowcase? 🛏️ weekly / monthly / ...never

source_quotes.aafa: Dust mites are too small to see with your eyes alone. They are only about one-quarter to one-third of a millimeter. Under a microscope, they look like white bugs. They have eight legs and are related to spiders. Dust mites thrive in temperatures around 70° F and above. They also like humidity levels above 50%. ... They feed mainly on the tiny flakes of human skin that you shed each day. These flakes work their way deep into fabric items in your home, such as furniture, carpets, bedding (pillow and mattress), and stuffed toys.
source_quotes.ala: Dust mites are very small, insect-like pests that feed on dead human skin cells and thrive in warm, humid settings. Dust mites are too small for us to see. They are not parasites that bite, sting or burrow into our bodies. ... Dust mites can live in bedding, mattresses, upholstered furniture, carpets and curtains. ... Wash bedding in hot water (at least 120 degrees F) once a week to kill and wash away dust mites.
source_quotes.wsu: House dust mites are extremely small (up to 0.5 mm) ... principally found in cotton-stuffed mattresses and furniture ... feed primarily on human skin cells that have sloughed off and pet dander. They do not bite. ... house dust mites prefer humid environments. ... Wash bedding regularly in hot water.
source_quotes.niehs: Dust mites are microscopic, insect-like pests that commonly live in house dust. They feed on flakes of dead skin, or dander, that are shed by people and pets. ... Dust mites can live in mattresses, bedding, upholstered furniture, carpets, and curtains in your home.
